summary: UC Riverside's Plant Biology PhD in the Department of Botany and Plant Sciences, with an early funding consideration deadline. Admitted PhD students are supported through assistantships, fellowships and scholarships.

deadlines.label: Deadline for department-paid application fee (domestic PhD applicants)
deadlines.note: Page: 'November 20, 2026 11:59 pm' for department-paid application fees (time zone not stated). This is a fee deadline, not the application deadline.

detailsNote: Official information available; the application deadlines (December 1 for fellowship consideration, June 1 admission-only) have no year stated on the page, so Fall 2027 is not confirmed. The admission model is not stated, so it is left out.

publishedDeadlines.note: Page lists Fall - December 1 (Fellowship Consideration) for domestic and international applicants. No year is given. Confirm Fall 2027 directly.

publishedDeadlines.label: Admission only, domestic, fall (no year stated)
publishedDeadlines.note: Page lists domestic Fall - June 1st (Admission Only). No year is given.

publishedDeadlines.note: Page lists November 20th as the Deadline for Early Funding Consideration for Fall Quarter. No year is given.

english.note: TOEFL scores are required of international students; no program-specific minimum is stated. UCR Graduate Division minimums: IELTS Academic overall 7 with no component below 6. Exemption for degrees from institutions where English is the sole language of instruction.

applicationFee.note: The department pays the fee for qualifying domestic Plant Biology PhD applicants (for example cumulative GPA of 3.3 or higher). UCR Graduate Division: 'Only U.S. Citizens and U.S. Permanent Residents may request a waiver for the application fee.' The 2027-28 hardship waiver form opened October 1, 2026. Correction checked 2026-10-29: central Summer 2024–Spring 2027 table lists international 155 USD versus domestic 135; Fall 2027 amount not confirmed.

requirements.note: Entry prerequisites include general biology, general chemistry, genetics, calculus, biochemistry or ecology, statistics and plant biology courses; missing courses can be taken after entry.

funding.note: Page: all PhD students admitted are supported by research assistantships, scholarships, teaching assistantships or fellowships, 'or (for foreign students) by grants from other countries or international agencies'. No amounts are stated.
